clue.text: Bags finally skiing silver in winter sport

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows
the first pair of pieces sit inside the sporting word that follows

blocks.note: the luge is a sled raced feet first down an ice track
last letter of skiing
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A skier finishing with a silver medal at a winter sports event bags the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' looks like a verb meaning wins, but it is the noun for travel cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags and suitcases carried on a journey are collectively called luggage.

clue.text: Makes sense to have a lot of gin in pub

definitions.note: verb phrase for an adjective; read as 'is logical'

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes
the shortened spirit is placed inside the word for a pub

blocks.note: a local is one's regular neighbourhood pub
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Someone justifies drinking plenty of gin down at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for the pub nearest home. 'Makes sense' stands for 'is logical'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that makes sense is reasonable and coherent, which is what logical describes.

clue.text: German party takes horse-drawn cart up to cemetery

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
a rave is a large dance party
a dray is a low cart pulled by horses, used by brewers

explanation.surface: A German celebration loads up a horse cart for a trip to the cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAY reversed gives YARD, so G + RAVE + YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard is a burial ground, the same as a cemetery.

clue.text: It holds food suspended when photo's taken

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: Someone holds a plate of food still in midair while a photograph is snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly in which pieces of meat, egg or vegetables are set and held in place.

clue.text: Drug's ten pounds? Even divvied, it's pricey

indicators.note: even here means the letters in the second, fourth and sixth positions

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
X is the Roman numeral for ten
pounds are enclosures for animals
the even-placed letters of divvied

explanation.surface: Even split among friends, ten pounds' worth of drugs is costly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' suggests money; here it means animal pens. E + X + PENS + IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pricey is an informal adjective for costly, meaning the same as expensive.

clue.text: Bison maybe? Expert has a look

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
taken as written
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A wildlife expert takes a look at what might be a bison.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bison is commonly called a buffalo, so a bison is one example of the name.

clue.text: Game with house to win?

blocks.note: surface reading: a casino game where the house is the opponent you hope to beat
setter's reading: house is the call made by the player who fills a card in this numbers game

explanation.walkthrough: In casinos the house always wins, so the clue suggests a game against the bank; in fact shouting 'House!' is how you claim the win in a hall game of numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game in which the winner calls out 'house' on completing a full card.

clue.text: Large risk? Not likely!

blocks.note: fat means large in girth
to chance something is to risk it

explanation.surface: A big gamble is dismissed as hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses sarcastic disbelief, meaning there is little or no possibility, just like the exclamation.

clue.text: Expect a humorist to collect top award

indicators.note: collecting something means taking it in, so the humorist holds a letter
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a wit is a person known for clever humour
first letter of award

explanation.surface: A comedian anticipates winning the top prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The humorist collects only the award's initial; the opening 'a' stays outside, in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it in anticipation, which is to expect it.

clue.text: Obviously young support liberal revolt

indicators.note: liberal suggests free and loose, so the letters can be freely rearranged
in a down clue a supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes last

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Y is the abbreviation for young

explanation.surface: Youth openly back a free-thinking uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks political but is the signal to rearrange; 'support' puts Y at the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtly means openly and without concealment, so plainly or obviously.

clue.text: Get hold of key file

blocks.note: G is a musical key
a rasp is a coarse file for wood or metal

explanation.surface: Someone needs to obtain an important computer file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key file' reads like an important document; key is a musical key and file the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp is to seize firmly in the hand, which is to get hold of something.

clue.text: Enter parking space in Paris and get charge

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
an en is a printer's space, half an em wide
et is the French word for and
a rate is a fixed charge or fee

explanation.surface: A driver finds a parking spot in Paris and has to pay for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space in Paris' looks like one phrase, but 'in Paris' belongs to 'and'. The en is a typesetting space.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate is to pass into or through something, which is to enter it.

clue.text: End soccer career on a high

indicators.note: to career is to rush about wildly, so the letters hurtle into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of both words, taken together

explanation.surface: A footballer retires from the game at the peak of their powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun, a working life, but it is the verb for careering about.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is the climax or peak point of something, a high.

clue.text: Start playing and thrash Italy

blocks.note: to thrash is to hit hard
IT is the international code for Italy

explanation.surface: A team kicks off and beats Italy soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a band's cue to begin performing music, the same as starting to play.

clue.text: Skipped exercise on field

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another follows it

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow or field
PT stands for physical training

explanation.surface: A pupil missed a games lesson out on the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipped' suggests missing a class; it is the past tense of jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip is to hop or bound, so skipped and leapt both mean jumped.

clue.text: For example, Chessington's motif has pirate's head on old ship

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter

blocks.note: a motif is a recurring theme
first letter of pirate
Noah's ark is the famous old ship

explanation.surface: An amusement park's pirate theme features a captain on a vintage vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Chessington World of Adventures is a theme park in Surrey, southwest of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chessington is one example of an amusement park built around themed rides and attractions.

clue.text: Get in uni abroad, taking first year with skill

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered far and wide, so the letters are thrown into a new order
first points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
first letter of year

explanation.surface: A student gets into a foreign university and takes a gap year cleverly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' joins the year's initial to the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingenuity is inventive cleverness, a kind of skill in solving problems.

clue.text: Harvests and sorts the grain around the beginning of September

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange into a new order
around means the rearranged letters surround a single letter
a word's beginning is its first letter

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
first letter of September

explanation.surface: A farmer reaps and sorts the grain at the start of September.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters GATHER-IN take S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in crops is to bring them in from the fields, which is what harvesting means.

clue.text: Set up society

blocks.note: first meaning: to establish or found something
second meaning: an organisation for a particular purpose

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like founding a club; the two parts are a verb and a noun for the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to establish, and as a noun it means an organised body or learned society.

clue.text: Get soldiers in after Trump briefly gives order

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped
the troops are placed inside the verb at the start of the clue
after means the first part of the clue is placed behind what follows

blocks.note: Judd Trump is an English snooker champion
taken as written
soldiers are men

explanation.surface: Once the president has spoken, the troops go in.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is not the US president but Judd Trump, the snooker player, 2019 world champion. JUD + GE(MEN)T.
explanation.definitionFit: A judgement is a court's ruling or decision, which is a kind of order.

clue.text: Boy by first light striking north to see bird

indicators.note: striking here means striking out, crossing a letter off

blocks.note: Jack is a boy's name
dawn is the first light of day
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A boy at daybreak heads north to watch a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: DAWN loses its N, leaving DAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a small grey-naped crow, a common bird of Europe.

clue.text: Art supporter left after rest

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second

blocks.note: ease is relaxation or rest
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A patron of the arts departed after a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art supporter' suggests a patron; it is literal, the stand that supports a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds up a canvas while it is painted.

clue.text: No pins to be hammered

blocks.note: first meaning: pins is slang for legs, so without any
second meaning: British slang for very drunk

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests carpentry with no pins to hammer in. Both pins (legs) and legless (too drunk to stand) are informal British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking legs is literally the word, and both it and hammered are slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Large number yearn to find hidden treasure

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
to ache for something is to yearn for it

explanation.surface: Many people long to discover buried treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a secret store of valuables, a hoard of hidden treasure.

clue.text: Ipecac tincture contains desert plants

indicators.note: contains says the answer is held within the run of letters before it

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A medicinal tincture is made from desert plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Ipecac is a plant-based emetic medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cacti are spiny succulent plants that thrive in deserts.

clue.text: Suppression of heartless monarch by church has popular backing at last

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter is removed
at last points to the final letter of the word

blocks.note: a queen is a female monarch
CH is the abbreviation for church
in means fashionable or popular
last letter of backing

explanation.surface: A cruel ruler is crushed by the church, which has finally won public support.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEEN loses its middle E to give QUEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Quenching a fire or a rebellion means putting it out, which is a suppression.

clue.text: Repeat question on love note

blocks.note: QU is short for question
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a query written on a love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote someone is to repeat their words exactly.

clue.text: Applaud men coming in to immobilise car

indicators.note: coming in means the second piece goes inside the first

blocks.note: to clap is to applaud
M is short for men, as on a toilet door

explanation.surface: Bystanders cheer as attendants arrive to lock a vehicle's wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: A wheel clamp is fitted to an illegally parked car to stop it being driven.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting a wheel clamp to a car stops it moving, so to clamp is to immobilise it.

clue.text: Drastic action to put in autocrats

indicators.note: putting letters into action sets them moving into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Extreme measures are needed to install strongmen in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drastic action' reads as one phrase; the first word is fodder and the second the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocrats rule with absolute power, which is what dictators are.

clue.text: Street maps have your report in colour

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the A-Z is a well-known British street atlas
the possessive said out loud

explanation.surface: City maps include a colour key for the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The A to Z is the standard London street atlas. AZ + URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky-blue shade, a colour.

clue.text: Crow's foot right inside shellfish

indicators.note: inside places the first piece within the sea creature

blocks.note: a winkle is a small edible sea snail
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bird's claw ends up inside a sea snail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow's foot' looks like a bird's foot; it is the line at the corner of an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's feet are the fine creases at the outer corner of the eyes, a kind of facial line.

clue.text: Writer's back and she's working to describe women family members

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from right to left
working suggests being worked over into a different shape
to describe is to draw around, so these letters enclose another

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: An author returns while she is busy writing about female relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Women family members' looks like the definition, but nephews are male; 'women' gives W inside the reworked SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nephews are the sons of one's siblings, so they are relatives or family members.
